authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Aquarius Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Aquarius, that may be the friendship that only works because one person keeps organizing everything, the group plan everyone agrees with but no one supports, or the role you accepted years ago that no one has checked to see if you still want.

Aquarius is a fixed air sign ruled by Saturn. It can step back from the immediate emotion and see how the larger system works. Who makes the decisions? Who carries the responsibility? Who is expected to adjust? That distance is useful when you need to see the pattern clearly. Taken too far, it can become detachment, rigid thinking, or loyalty to a principle long after it stops helping the people involved.

The Sun in Leo sits opposite this Moon, bringing personal recognition into tension with the expectations of the group. You may notice where you have been waiting for approval, staying loyal to a familiar role, or agreeing with a plan because you do not want to risk your place in the room. If belonging depends on staying quiet or continuing to play the same part, that arrangement becomes harder to defend. You may also see where a group has been happy to use your work while treating your need for credit as an ego problem.

Saturn gives this Full Moon weight. The problem probably did not begin this week. It may be the same limitation everyone keeps working around, the responsibility that keeps returning to the same person, or the future plan that still sounds good but has no budget, deadline, or clear owner.

Clarity does not require a decision on the same day. Let the information settle. Notice what needs new terms, what both sides are willing to repair, and what has reached its limit.
source_keys: TLDR-Lunation-Blend-Units-V1.md

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Aquarius New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
An Aquarius New Moon tends to arrive when everyone already agrees the old arrangement is broken, and nobody wants the uncomfortable work of writing down what changes. The group announces a fresh start, the project gets a new title, the relationship claims new rules, and the actual labor stays exactly where it was.

Aquarius is a fixed air sign ruled by Saturn, so this beginning is not the rush of an exciting idea; it is the structure required to sustain one. If the plan only works while one person quietly absorbs everyone else's inconvenience, it is not collaboration. It is the old deal wearing a new name.

Saturn gives this start a long clock. Progress looks quiet at first because the foundation has to hold real weight, and a plan that survives only while nobody asks a hard question is already failing. The Aquarius shadow is distance: it is possible to analyze the system brilliantly and miss the people being worn down inside it.

Write the terms down while the start is still small. Six months from now, the results will not remember anyone's intentions. They will show which agreements were actually kept.

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Leo New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. In Leo, those terms are personal. This beginning will not function as a committee decision, an audience poll, or a favor to keep someone else comfortable. It has to be owned, signed, and visibly yours.

Leo is fixed fire ruled by the Sun. The Sun is at home here, which means the only start it honors is the one driven by genuine, unmanufactured desire. Ask yourself what you would still build if nobody was watching, and what you would refuse to abandon the moment public attention moves elsewhere. That is the test to run before you commit. Strip the audience away: if the work still feels vital, it is yours; if it goes cold, you were doing it for applause.

The shadow here is defensive pride. Leo energy wants to protect a plan early, sometimes long before there is an actual result to show for it. Validation feels good, but it makes a hollow foundation.

Start the project that carries your name comfortably. When the work is genuinely yours, you never have to spend your energy defending its right to exist.

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Pisces Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Pisces, what surfaces is usually whatever you have been absorbing without keeping score: the temporary help that turned into a permanent obligation, the empathy that became unpaid emotional labor, or the vague arrangement that drifted for months because naming the boundary felt unkind.

Pisces is a mutable water sign ruled by Jupiter, the planet of scale, belief, and generosity. That traditional rulership matters: this sign gives, forgives, and insists on finding a deeper meaning where other signs would just see a loss. At its best, that is faith working as designed. Taken too far, it is a refusal to look at plain facts because the fantasy version feels safer.

The Sun in Virgo sits directly opposite this Moon, holding the practical line: the budget, the physical body, the actual calendar, the real cost. The tension here is not between hope and cynicism; it is between what you want to believe about a situation and what you can actually verify.

Check the details without treating reality as a betrayal of the dream. What survives an honest look deserves your faith; what depended on vagueness to survive was already gone.

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Virgo New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. A Virgo New Moon begins with the checklist. This is the sky for unglamorous progress: the health requirement entered into the calendar, the backlog finally cleared, or the daily workflow rebuilt so the same crisis stops arriving every Thursday. Nothing here needs a public announcement. It just works better inside of a month.

Virgo is a mutable earth sign ruled by Mercury, operating here on precision over speed: test, adjust, and evaluate. A Virgo start is intentionally small. It knows a system shifts through its micro-details, and it distrusts any grand plan too large to test this week.

The trap is perfectionism as an avoidance tactic. Optimization can become its own endless project, and a standard set impossibly high functions identically to never starting at all. Flawlessness is not on the menu; small, repeated corrections are the entire method.

Pick one daily process and improve it by one concrete step. Small is not a compromise here; small is the actual design.

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Aries New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. In Aries, the terms are speed and ownership: this beginning belongs to whoever moves first, and it loses power every day it waits for a better moment. The right start here is closer to a first step than a plan.

Aries is cardinal fire ruled by Mars. The beginning it favors is direct: ask the person, send the application, sign up, start training. Mars does not negotiate with hesitation; it converts it into frustration, and frustration into either action or resentment.

The risk is the false start. Aries opens strong and delegates the follow-through to a future self who never agreed to it. Do not confuse the rush of deciding with the work of doing.

Start one concrete effort this week and give it a move you can finish before the weekend. Momentum is easier to keep than to restart.

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Taurus New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. In Taurus, the terms are material: what this costs, what it pays, and if the pace can be kept for months without breaking what already works. The beginning it favors is slow, physical, and built to last.

Taurus is fixed earth ruled by Venus, so the start has to feel good to survive: the routine you would keep even on a bad week, the purchase that still makes sense in a year, the work your body does not dread. Pleasure here is not indulgence; it is the maintenance plan.

The risk is refusing to start at all because the current arrangement is comfortable enough. Comfort can preserve a life that has quietly stopped fitting.

Begin the slow build: one asset, one habit, one commitment with a long horizon. Choose what you are willing to repeat, because repetition is the whole method.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Gemini New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. In Gemini, the terms are curiosity and contact: the question you finally ask, the course you sample, the conversation that changes what you know.

Gemini is mutable air ruled by Mercury. This beginning does not need certainty; it needs correspondence: send the message, book the call, read the first chapter, talk to the person who has already done it. Information moves first here and commitment follows.

The risk is scattering: five beginnings, each two days deep, none with a second week.

Pick two threads at most and give both a next step. In Gemini the follow-up question is worth more than the brilliant first one.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Cancer New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. In Cancer, the terms are belonging: who is inside the wall, what home is supposed to provide, and which people get your protection without applying for it. (Engine note: the Moon rules its own lunation here; skip rule active, no ruler line.)

Cancer is cardinal water ruled by the Moon, and the beginning it favors is close to home: the household change, the family conversation, the decision about where and with whom you actually live. Feelings are the evidence this start runs on, and they are admissible.

The risk is the shell: protecting so carefully that nothing new is allowed in, including the good. Safety that cannot be updated becomes a smaller life than the one you were protecting.

Begin where you live: the home repair, the standing dinner, the boundary that makes your place feel like yours again.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Libra New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. In Libra, the terms are mutual: this beginning involves another person, and it works only if the deal is stated instead of assumed.

Libra is cardinal air ruled by Venus. The start it favors is relational and explicit: the partnership formalized, the collaboration proposed, the conflict opened politely on purpose. Fair terms at the start save the renegotiation later.

The risk is agreeableness: beginning what the other person wants and calling the relief of their approval a decision. A partnership begun on unstated terms is an argument on a delay timer.

Open the conversation you have been balancing in your head. Say the terms first; adjust them together second.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Scorpio New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. In Scorpio, the terms are total: this beginning is private, deliberate, and it requires telling yourself the truth before anyone else hears the plan.

Scorpio is fixed water ruled by Mars, the planet of pursuit: beneath the stillness, this sign hunts. The start it favors runs deep and quiet: the debt payoff mapped, the therapy begun, the merger of money or lives negotiated for real, the decision made once and not reopened.

The risk is control: waiting for guaranteed terms that never arrive, or starting a hidden version of the plan so no one can watch it fail.

Commit fully in private first. What begins with your whole agreement does not need witnesses to hold.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Sagittarius New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. In Sagittarius, the terms are size: this beginning has to be worth the story you will tell about it. Small maintenance starts do not hold here; a direction does.

Sagittarius is mutable fire ruled by Jupiter. The start it favors points at a horizon: the trip booked, the course of study entered, the belief tested in the world instead of defended at home. Optimism is legitimate fuel here.

The risk is the launch with no landing gear: enthusiasm that signs up for everything and completes the first tenth. A vision without a first concrete leg is a mood.

Choose the destination, then buy the first ticket only. The rest of the route can adapt; the departure cannot keep moving.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Capricorn New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. In Capricorn, the terms are structural: what is being built, who is responsible, and what it costs per month in effort you can actually supply.

Capricorn is cardinal earth ruled by Saturn, at home and unsentimental. The beginning it favors has a foundation poured before the announcement: the business registered, the certification begun, the savings plan automated. Ambition here is a schedule, not a feeling.

The risk is postponement disguised as preparation, and its twin: building the impressive structure on top of a life with no rest in it.

Lay one foundation stone this month, on a timeline you would show a skeptic. What is built properly here tends to still be standing years later.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Pisces New Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
New Moons begin a six-month cycle, and what starts now grows on the terms you set first. In Pisces, the terms are quiet: this beginning starts as a pull rather than a plan, and it needs protecting from ridicule while it is still soft.

Pisces is mutable water ruled by Jupiter, which gives even this gentle sign a size: the creative practice, the spiritual commitment, the act of service that grows past its container. Begin before you can explain it; explanation arrives later here.

The risk is drift: a beginning that stays a feeling, comforted instead of started. Vagueness can protect a dream and starve it with the same gesture.

Give the pull one scheduled hour a week and a place where nobody grades it. What is real will use the hour.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Aries Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Aries, what surfaces is anger with a history: the accommodation that went one direction for months, the independence traded away in small, reasonable-sounding pieces, the self that got manageable to keep a peace nobody else was keeping.

Aries is cardinal fire ruled by Mars, so what comes up now does not arrive politely. The heat is data: it points at the exact place a limit was crossed and nobody said so.

The Sun in Libra holds the other end: the relationship, the agreement, the appearance of harmony. The tension is not selfishness against love. It is if the current terms require one person to disappear in installments.

Say the direct sentence. Anger that gets a clear channel becomes a boundary; anger that does not becomes an ambush later.

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Taurus Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Taurus, what surfaces is the physical truth: what the body has been carrying, what the money has actually been doing, which comforts calm you and which ones just sedate the question.

Taurus is fixed earth ruled by Venus. What comes into view is the difference between owning your possessions and being owned by their maintenance, between stability and the fear of moving.

The Sun in Scorpio holds the other end: the shared, the merged, the emotionally expensive. The tension runs between keeping what is yours and the intimacy that requires risking some of it.

Keep what your hands actually use and your body actually rests in. What you keep out of fear owns you back.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Gemini Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Gemini, what surfaces is the unsaid backlog: the conversation postponed into a private monologue, the facts collected but never assembled, the two versions of the story you tell depending on the listener.

Gemini is mutable air ruled by Mercury: the pressure here is verbal, and it breaks as words: the message finally sent, the question finally asked in plain terms, the sentence you have rehearsed for a month said in fifteen seconds.

The Sun in Sagittarius holds the other end: the big claim, the belief, the meaning of it all. The tension is between the details you know and the story you have been telling over them.

Say the specific sentence, not the speech. One accurate detail moves more than the whole defended narrative.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Cancer Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Cancer, what surfaces is what home has actually been costing: the care that runs one direction, the family role assigned before you could object, the difference between the place you live and a place that restores you. (Engine note: the Moon rules its own lunation here; skip rule active, no ruler line.)

Cancer is cardinal water ruled by the Moon, at full strength in its own sign: feelings arrive at high tide, and they are accurate about what they concern even when loud about how.

The Sun in Capricorn holds the other end: the job, the obligations, the version of you that functions in public. The tension is the oldest one: the life you maintain against the people and comfort it was supposed to be for.

Feed the actual home: the person, the ritual, the reconciliation. Duty that never comes home is just employment.

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Leo Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Leo, what surfaces is the need to be seen specifically, not generally: the credit that went to the group, the effort mistaken for ego the moment it asked for acknowledgment, the warmth you stopped showing because it was mistaken for neediness. (Engine note: the Sun rules Leo and participates in every lunation; skip rule active, no ruler line.)

Leo is fixed fire ruled by the Sun. What rises now is personal pride, and pride is not the flaw here; the hiding is. A heart that performs modesty long enough starts believing the diminished version.

The Sun in Aquarius holds the other end: the group, the cause, the collective schedule. The tension is between mattering as a person and functioning as a member.

Take the credit that has your name on it, and give the specific praise you have been rationing. Recognition is not a scarce resource; treating it like one is the actual problem.

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Virgo Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Virgo, what surfaces is the invisible workload: the corrections nobody sees, the standards nobody else maintains, the sense that keeping everything working has quietly become your unpaid second job.

Virgo is mutable earth ruled by Mercury: the details rise now, itemized. The question they document is not if you are useful. It is what the usefulness is costing, and who looks after the person who checks on everything.

The Sun in Pisces holds the other end: rest, faith, the unmeasured life. The tension is between the fixable and the acceptable, between service and dissolving into other people's needs.

Retire two obligations that exist only because you never said no to them. Precision about your own limits is also a skill.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Libra Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Libra, what surfaces is the price of balance: the opinions traded for approval, the conflict avoided so long it matured into distance, the relationship maintained by exactly one person's flexibility.

Libra is cardinal air ruled by Venus. What becomes visible is the difference between peace and quiet: peace has been negotiated; quiet has just been enforced by whoever minds least.

The Sun in Aries holds the other end: the self, the want, the direct move. The tension is between being fair and being present, because a partner who has vanished into accommodation is not actually in the relationship.

Reopen one negotiation honestly. A relationship that cannot survive your actual preferences is not being protected; it is being postponed.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Scorpio Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Scorpio, what surfaces is what the arrangement really runs on: who holds the power, who holds the information, and which loyalty is love and which is collateral.

Scorpio is fixed water ruled by Mars: what rises now was pursued and buried on purpose, and it comes back with receipts: the resentment with a start date, the secret with a shelf life, the desire that did not dissolve just because it was inconvenient.

The Sun in Taurus holds the other end: the simple, the ownable, the calm. The tension is between the depth that makes intimacy real and the peace that makes daily life possible.

Name one buried term of the arrangement to the other person in it. What is spoken can be renegotiated; what stays buried collects interest.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Sagittarius Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Sagittarius, what surfaces is the gap between the philosophy and the itinerary: the freedom talked about and not scheduled, the belief announced and not lived, the promise that the real life starts after this next stretch.

Sagittarius is mutable fire ruled by Jupiter: what rises is appetite for meaning, and it will indict a comfortable routine without hesitation.

The Sun in Gemini holds the other end: the daily facts, the small commitments, the calendar as it actually looks. The tension is between the story of your life and its schedule, and only one of them is currently true.

Book the concrete version of one belief: the trip, the course, the conversation with the mentor. A philosophy with no departure date is a decoration.
source_keys: Lunation fallback set — full sign coverage, 19 macros + 20 compact cores

authoredCards.headline: The Macro View: What the Capricorn Full Moon Represents
authoredCards.body:
Full Moons bring what has been building into clearer view. In Capricorn, what surfaces is the bill for the climb: the title that costs the evenings, the responsibility that was temporary two years ago, the reputation maintained at the expense of the person maintaining it.

Capricorn is cardinal earth ruled by Saturn, and what rises now is structural: which ambitions are load-bearing and which are just heavy.

The Sun in Cancer holds the other end: home, family, the life the work was supposed to fund. The tension is between the mountain and the reason you started climbing it.

Renegotiate one standing obligation before it renews by default. The career that costs the whole life is not success; it is an unexamined contract.

hookRows.body_you:
A Leo New Moon is for starting what you actually want, not the diluted version you present to look reasonable. The Sun rules Leo, so this beginning runs on honest desire: the project you choose in private, the authority you stop waiting for someone to hand you, or the creative pleasure you restore to a life that has turned into pure maintenance.

This is where you give concrete hours to work that carries your imprint, claim space without apologizing for it, and stop hiding your ambition behind humility. Fixed fire commits from the heart, and it holds its ground. That is the strength and the warning: choose carefully, because what you start here will stick.

The trap is performing for an audience. If you cannot name what you want without checking who is watching, you are not ready to begin. What would you build if nobody ever saw the middle?

hookRows.body_you:
A Pisces Full Moon shows you exactly where the story you tell yourself and the reality on the ground have split apart. Jupiter rules Pisces, so the spotlight hits faith, generosity, and the excuses that keep an unsustainable situation running: the potential you keep extending credit to, the person you describe by who they could be instead of who they are, or the sacrifice that runs on habit rather than love.

You may realize you have been quietly paying the entire bill: covering the difference, softening the impact, and translating someone else's silence into reassurance. Compassion takes real energy, and Pisces gives it away without a timesheet. That is why the total cost shocks you when it finally lands.

Mutable water does not force a dramatic fight; it simply stops feeding what gives nothing back. Which parts of the dream hold up when you state them in plain facts? Keep those. Whatever you can only defend in soft focus is already over.

hookRows.body_you: A Virgo New Moon starts small and practical on purpose. Mercury rules this sign, making the beginning a routine, not a speech: one fix, one boundary, one measurable change. What gets quietly repaired this month lasts.

hookRows.body_you:
A Virgo New Moon is for fixing what you have been working around. Mercury rules Virgo, so the starting line is concrete and specific: the daily routine you rebuild, the appointment you stop rescheduling, or the recurring problem you solve at the source instead of managing every afternoon.

This is the health habit started at a scale your body can actually sustain, the workspace cleared so your daily labor stops fighting clutter, or the cold comparison of where your time actually goes versus where you claim it goes.

The shadow is relentless self-criticism. Virgo spots the flaw immediately, and turned inward without boundaries, that skill turns a fresh start into an inventory of personal failures. You are not a project to be debugged. Pick one practical process, make it five percent better, and let the result speak for itself. What is the one small fix you keep postponing because it is not impressive enough to post about? Start there.
